question: In the Basic Control Skills test, what is defined as a "pull-up"?
choice_a: Pulling forward on a backing exercise to clear an encroachment or get a better position
choice_b: Touching a boundary cone with the vehicle's mirror
choice_c: Exiting the vehicle to check its position
choice_d: Stopping the vehicle without changing direction
explanation: The manual defines a pull-up as pulling forward on a backing exercise to clear an encroachment or get a better position; stopping without changing direction does not count as a pull-up.
source_note: Utah CDL Manual, Section 12.1 - Basic Control Skills Test Scoring

question: What is scored as an "encroachment" during a Basic Control Skills exercise?
choice_a: Pulling the vehicle forward to gain a better position
choice_b: Touching or crossing an exercise boundary line or cone with any part of the vehicle other than mirrors or unique parts at or above door-mirror height
choice_c: Exiting the vehicle to check its position while backing
choice_d: Sounding the horn before completing the exercise
explanation: The manual defines an encroachment as touching or crossing an exercise boundary line or cone with any part of the vehicle other than the mirrors (or unique parts at/above door mirror height).
source_note: Utah CDL Manual, Section 12.1 - Basic Control Skills Test Scoring

question: What action is scored as a "look" during a Basic Control Skills exercise?
choice_a: Using the turn signal before backing
choice_b: Crossing over a boundary cone with the vehicle
choice_c: Opening the door or moving from a seated position while in physical control of the vehicle (or, on a bus, walking to the back for a better view)
choice_d: Pulling forward to correct the vehicle's position
explanation: The manual states that opening the door or moving from a seated position while in physical control of the vehicle (or walking to the back on a bus) is scored as a look.
source_note: Utah CDL Manual, Section 12.1 - Basic Control Skills Test Scoring

question: The manual states the driver will be scored for "final position" on which two exercises?
choice_a: Exercise 1 (Forward Stop) and Exercise 3 (Forward Offset Tracking)
choice_b: Exercise 1 (Forward Stop) and Exercise 4 (Reverse Offset Backing)
choice_c: Exercise 2 (Straight-Line Backing) and Exercise 3 (Forward Offset Tracking)
choice_d: Exercise 2 (Straight-Line Backing) and Exercise 4 (Reverse Offset Backing)
explanation: Final position is scored on Exercise 2, Straight-Line Backing, and Exercise 4, Reverse Offset Backing.
source_note: Utah CDL Manual, Section 12.1 - Basic Control Skills Test Scoring

question: How many free looks may a candidate use on Exercise 2, Straight-Line Backing, to check the vehicle's position?
choice_a: One
choice_b: Two
choice_c: Three
choice_d: Zero
explanation: The manual allows a maximum of one free look on Exercise 2, Straight-Line Backing.
source_note: Utah CDL Manual, Section 12.1 - Basic Control Skills Test Scoring

question: How many free looks may a candidate use on Exercise 4, Reverse Offset Backing?
choice_a: One
choice_b: Two
choice_c: Zero
choice_d: Unlimited, as long as it's done safely
explanation: The manual allows a maximum of two free looks on Exercise 4, Reverse Offset Backing.
source_note: Utah CDL Manual, Section 12.1 - Basic Control Skills Test Scoring

question: Before safely exiting the vehicle to check its position during a backing exercise, what must the candidate first do?
choice_a: Sound the horn twice and wave to the examiner
choice_b: Turn on the four-way emergency flashers
choice_c: Set the parking brake(s) and place the vehicle in neutral/park
choice_d: Ask the examiner for a hand signal
explanation: The manual requires the driver to set the parking brake(s) and place the vehicle in neutral/park before safely exiting to check the vehicle's position.
source_note: Utah CDL Manual, Section 12.1 - Basic Control Skills Test Scoring

topic: Basic Control Skills Scoring / Unsafe Act
question: What may result if a candidate opens the vehicle door while the vehicle is still moving (not in neutral/park)?
choice_a: A single encroachment error
choice_b: Only a verbal warning from the examiner
choice_c: Loss of one free look
choice_d: Automatic failure for an unsafe act
explanation: The manual states that opening the door while the vehicle is moving may result in an automatic failure for an unsafe act.
source_note: Utah CDL Manual, Section 12.1 - Basic Control Skills Test Scoring

question: Exercise 1, Forward Stop, requires the candidate to demonstrate what skill?
choice_a: Judging the front of the vehicle during a controlled stop, stopping the front-most part within a box at the end of the alley
choice_b: Backing the vehicle in a straight line through an alley
choice_c: Maneuvering around objects while moving forward without stopping
choice_d: Offset backing and parking within three feet of the alley's rear
explanation: Exercise 1, Forward Stop, requires the driver to judge the front of the vehicle during a controlled stop, stopping the front-most part within the box at the end of the alley.
source_note: Utah CDL Manual, Section 12.2.1 - Exercise 1, Forward Stop

question: During Exercise 1, Forward Stop, how many times may the candidate stop the vehicle?
choice_a: As many times as needed to align correctly
choice_b: Only once
choice_c: Up to two times
choice_d: Up to three times
explanation: The manual states the candidate may stop only once during Exercise 1, Forward Stop.
source_note: Utah CDL Manual, Section 12.2.1 - Exercise 1, Forward Stop

question: During Exercise 2, Straight-Line Backing, how many free pull-ups and vehicle exits are the candidate allowed?
choice_a: Two free pull-ups and two exits
choice_b: Zero free pull-ups and two exits
choice_c: One free pull-up and one exit to check around the vehicle
choice_d: Unlimited pull-ups but zero exits
explanation: The manual allows one free pull-up and permits the candidate to safely exit the vehicle only one time to check around it during Exercise 2.
source_note: Utah CDL Manual, Section 12.2.2 - Exercise 2, Straight Line Backing

question: Exercise 3, Forward Offset Tracking, requires the candidate to do what?
choice_a: Back straight through an alley until clearing the last set of cones
choice_b: Stop with the front-most part of the vehicle inside a box
choice_c: Offset back into an alley to within three feet of the rear
choice_d: Drive forward and steer left through an opening into the opposite lane without stopping
explanation: Exercise 3 requires the driver to drive forward and steer to the left through the opening into the opposite lane without stopping.
source_note: Utah CDL Manual, Section 12.2.3 - Exercise 3, Forward Offset Tracking

question: In Exercise 3, Forward Offset Tracking, the candidate is scored for keeping which part of the vehicle between the cone and the line?
choice_a: The right-most rear tire
choice_b: The front bumper
choice_c: The left mirror
choice_d: The steering axle
explanation: The manual scores forward tracking clearance based on keeping the right-most rear tire between the cone and the line.
source_note: Utah CDL Manual, Section 12.2.3 - Exercise 3, Forward Offset Tracking

question: Exercise 4, Reverse Offset Backing, requires the candidate to bring the rear-most part of the vehicle to within how many feet of the rear of the alley?
choice_a: One foot
choice_b: Three feet
choice_c: Five feet
choice_d: Ten feet
explanation: The manual requires the rear-most part of the vehicle to come within three feet of the rear of the alley in Exercise 4.
source_note: Utah CDL Manual, Section 12.2.4 - Exercise 4, Reverse Offset Backing

question: During Exercise 4, Reverse Offset Backing, how many free pull-ups and vehicle exits are allowed?
choice_a: One free pull-up and one exit
choice_b: Zero free pull-ups and unlimited exits
choice_c: Two free pull-ups and a maximum of two exits
choice_d: Three free pull-ups and three exits
explanation: The manual allows two free pull-ups and permits the candidate to exit the vehicle a maximum of two times during Exercise 4.
source_note: Utah CDL Manual, Section 12.2.4 - Exercise 4, Reverse Offset Backing

topic: Basic Control Skills Test Scoring Threshold
question: According to the Utah Driver License Division's official CDL driving test page, what is the maximum number of error points a candidate may accrue and still pass the Basic Control Skills test?
choice_a: Four or fewer
choice_b: Fifteen or fewer
choice_c: Twenty or fewer
choice_d: Eight or fewer
explanation: The Utah DLD's official CDL driving test page states that a candidate must accrue eight or fewer error points to pass the Basic Control Skills test.
source_note: dld.utah.gov/cdl-driving-test/

question: According to the Utah DLD, what is the maximum number of error points a candidate may accrue and still pass the on-road Driving Skills test?
choice_a: Thirty or fewer
choice_b: Eight or fewer
choice_c: Fifteen or fewer
choice_d: Forty-five or fewer
explanation: The Utah DLD's official CDL driving test page states that a candidate must accrue 30 or fewer error points to pass the on-road Driving Skills test.
source_note: dld.utah.gov/cdl-driving-test/

question: Which of the following is explicitly required of a candidate during the on-road driving test?
choice_a: Drive a route with no traffic signals
choice_b: Wear a safety belt and obey all traffic signs, signals, and laws
choice_c: Use only manual-transmission vehicles
choice_d: Complete the test in under 20 minutes
explanation: Section 13 requires the candidate to wear a safety belt, obey all traffic signs, signals, and laws, and complete the test without an accident or moving violation.
source_note: Utah CDL Manual, Section 13.1 - How You Will Be Tested

question: If the test route lacks a certain traffic situation, such as a railroad crossing, what may the examiner ask the candidate to do?
choice_a: Skip that scoring category entirely with no penalty
choice_b: Automatically fail that portion
choice_c: Simulate it by explaining what they are or would be doing in that situation
choice_d: Reschedule the test for a different route
explanation: The manual states that if a route lacks a traffic situation, the candidate may be asked to simulate it by telling the examiner what they are or would be doing.
source_note: Utah CDL Manual, Section 13.1 - How You Will Be Tested

question: How does the manual define "unsafe coasting" when approaching a turn?
choice_a: Braking too early before a stop line
choice_b: Failing to use a turn signal
choice_c: Shifting gears more than once during a turn
choice_d: The vehicle being out of gear (clutch depressed or gearshift in neutral) for more than the length of the vehicle
explanation: The manual defines unsafe coasting as the vehicle being out of gear, with the clutch depressed or gearshift in neutral, for more than the length of the vehicle.
source_note: Utah CDL Manual, Section 13.1.1 - Turns

question: While stopped and waiting to proceed through an intersection, what must the candidate's vehicle do?
choice_a: Not roll forward or backward
choice_b: Roll forward slightly to signal readiness
choice_c: Creep forward gradually
choice_d: Roll backward slightly, which is acceptable on inclines
explanation: The manual states the vehicle must not roll forward or backward while stopped at an intersection.
source_note: Utah CDL Manual, Section 13.1.2 - Intersections

question: During the "Urban Business" portion of the on-road test, where should the candidate's vehicle be positioned?
choice_a: Straddling the center line for visibility
choice_b: Centered in the proper lane, the right-most lane
choice_c: In the left-most lane to allow merging traffic
choice_d: In the center turn lane
explanation: The manual states the vehicle should be centered in the proper lane, the right-most lane, during the Urban Business portion of the test.
source_note: Utah CDL Manual, Section 13.1.3 - Urban Business

question: During the multiple-lane portion of the on-road test, what lane-change sequence is the candidate asked to perform?
choice_a: Change to the right only
choice_b: Change to the left only
choice_c: Change to the left, then back to the right, using proper checks and signals
choice_d: Change lanes twice to the left in succession
explanation: The manual states that during multiple-lane portions of the test, the candidate will be asked to change lanes to the left, and then back to the right.
source_note: Utah CDL Manual, Section 13.1.4 - Lane Changes

question: Before entering the expressway during the test, the candidate must check traffic, use proper signals, and do what else?
choice_a: Accelerate to maximum speed before merging
choice_b: Activate four-way flashers
choice_c: Come to a complete stop before merging
choice_d: Merge smoothly into the proper lane of traffic
explanation: The manual states that before entering the expressway, the candidate must check traffic, use proper signals, and merge smoothly into the proper lane of traffic.
source_note: Utah CDL Manual, Section 13.1.5 - Expressway or Rural/Limited Access Highway

question: Once on the expressway exit ramp, what must the candidate continue to do?
choice_a: Decelerate within the lane markings while maintaining adequate spacing from other vehicles
choice_b: Accelerate to match highway speed
choice_c: Change lanes to pass slower vehicles
choice_d: Activate the parking brake
explanation: The manual states that once on the exit ramp, the candidate must continue to decelerate within the lane markings and maintain adequate spacing between the vehicle and other vehicles.
source_note: Utah CDL Manual, Section 13.1.5 - Expressway or Rural/Limited Access Highway

question: During the Stop/Start maneuver, once the vehicle is stopped, which of the following must the candidate do?
choice_a: Restart the engine immediately
choice_b: Activate the four-way emergency flashers and apply the parking brake
choice_c: Exit the vehicle to inspect it
choice_d: Sound the horn
explanation: The manual requires the candidate to activate the four-way emergency flashers and apply the parking brake once stopped during the Stop/Start maneuver.
source_note: Utah CDL Manual, Section 13.1.6 - Stop/Start

question: When instructed to resume from the Stop/Start maneuver, what must the candidate do before pulling back into traffic?
choice_a: Immediately release the parking brake without checking traffic
choice_b: Turn the steering wheel before the vehicle moves
choice_c: Check traffic and mirrors thoroughly, turn off the four-way flashers, and activate the left turn signal
choice_d: Sound the horn continuously
explanation: The manual states that when resuming, the candidate must check traffic and mirrors thoroughly, turn off the four-way flashers, and activate the left turn signal before pulling back into traffic.
source_note: Utah CDL Manual, Section 13.1.6 - Stop/Start

question: When approaching a curve, the candidate should reduce speed before entering it so that what is not required in the curve?
choice_a: Steering
choice_b: Checking traffic
choice_c: Accelerating
choice_d: Further braking or shifting
explanation: The manual states that before entering the curve, the candidate should reduce speed so further braking or shifting is not required in the curve.
source_note: Utah CDL Manual, Section 13.1.7 - Curve

question: A bus, school bus, or vehicle displaying placards must stop within what distance range from the nearest rail at a railroad crossing?
choice_a: Within 50 feet but not less than 15 feet
choice_b: Within 100 feet but not less than 25 feet
choice_c: Within 30 feet but not less than 10 feet
choice_d: Exactly 20 feet
explanation: The manual states such vehicles must stop within 50 feet but not less than 15 feet from the nearest rail at a railroad crossing.
source_note: Utah CDL Manual, Section 13.1.8 - Railroad Crossing

question: While any part of the vehicle is proceeding across railroad tracks, the candidate must NOT do which of the following?
choice_a: Keep both hands on the steering wheel
choice_b: Stop, change gears, or change lanes
choice_c: Continue checking mirrors after crossing
choice_d: Deactivate four-way flashers after crossing
explanation: The manual states the driver must not stop, change gears, or change lanes while any part of the vehicle is proceeding across the tracks.
source_note: Utah CDL Manual, Section 13.1.8 - Railroad Crossing

question: After driving under an overpass during the test, what might the examiner ask the candidate to report?
choice_a: The color and material of the overpass
choice_b: The name of the road it carries
choice_c: The posted clearance or height
choice_d: The year the overpass was built
explanation: The manual states the candidate may be asked to tell the examiner what the posted clearance or height was after driving under an overpass.
source_note: Utah CDL Manual, Section 13.1.9 - Bridge/Overpass/Sign

question: When performing a student discharge for a School Bus endorsement, how far from the students at the stop must the bus come to a complete stop?
choice_a: At least 5 feet
choice_b: At least 15 feet
choice_c: At least 20 feet
choice_d: At least 10 feet
explanation: The manual requires the school bus to come to a complete stop at least 10 feet away from students at the stop.
source_note: Utah CDL Manual, Section 13.1.10 - Student Discharge (School Bus)

question: If a candidate is driving a vehicle with an unsynchronized manual transmission, what must they do when shifting?
choice_a: Double-clutch when shifting
choice_b: Single-clutch and rev the engine between shifts
choice_c: Ride the clutch to control speed
choice_d: Coast with the clutch depressed
explanation: The manual requires the candidate to double-clutch when shifting an unsynchronized manual transmission, and prohibits riding the clutch or coasting with it depressed.
source_note: Utah CDL Manual, Section 13.1.11(a) - Clutch Usage (for Manual Transmission)

question: On a multiple-lane road, in which lane should the candidate finish a left turn?
choice_a: The left-most lane available
choice_b: The lane directly to the right of the center line
choice_c: Any lane that is open at the time
choice_d: The curb (right-most) lane
explanation: The manual states the vehicle should finish a left turn in the lane directly to the right of the center line.
source_note: Utah CDL Manual, Section 13.1.14(d) - Lane Usage

topic: General Driving Behaviors - Use of Turn Signals
question: Per the General Driving Behaviors category on use of turn signals, when must the candidate cancel a turn signal?
choice_a: Only when reminded by the examiner
choice_b: Before completing the turn or lane change
choice_c: Upon completion of a turn or lane change
choice_d: Turn signals should never be cancelled manually
explanation: The manual states the candidate must cancel turn signals upon completion of a turn or lane change.
source_note: Utah CDL Manual, Section 13.1.17 - Use of Turn Signals
